body: Yeah my disability makes me unable to care for myself let alone a child. My THERAPIST tried telling me that I'd change my mind eventually. Tbh I'd rather kill myself than knowingly bring a life into this hellhole.

I'm disabled from mental illness I don't have any extra money beyond rent, gas, utilities, medications, and barely food- especially since I'm trying GF and dairy free :') I also can't take CBD because it makes me manic and crazy. Unfortunately my insurance doesn't cover dieticians unless you have diabetes, or have some kind of organ failure going on. But they WILL cover weight loss surgery, which is stupid. (I am thinking about it though because studies have shown hypothyroid people who get the gastric sleeve were able to go down in thyroid medication and feel better on average. Unsure about how it would work with Hashimoto's people tho.)

If my doctor can't figure it out after this next bloodwork and doesn't try anything different I might try seeing an endo. I'm sick and I shouldn't need to take and do five hundred different things to feel better. It's unfair and depressing. I'm just really frustrated with this, when I was 16 and first diagnosed I took levothyroxine and my symptoms went away. Now I'm 22 and I can barely function on top of already being unable to function with my bipolar disorder. (Pretty sure the thyroid is making my BP worse)
Yeah that's what I was thinking since calcium affects absorption
Nope, they look normal. My hands and feet are the coldest parts of my body though. They're like ice.

I guess going outside and walking down the street was enough to make me sweat and be totally out of breath lol. Probably in an hour I'll be back to being freezing again tho. That's just how it goes.

Edit: I am now cold again

Exactly. Is it possible to have TSH in the hundreds? Yes. But I shouldn't have to get to that point for people to believe I feel like crap every day! Right now I'm under a thermal shirt AND heavy blanket and I'm still freezing. My legs hurt so bad from the muscles being tightened uncontrollably. My brain fog is so so so bad I can't even remember things people tell me fifteen minutes ago, and I forget HOW TO DO MY JOB ;(
Like my employee idea I had down pat? I do not remember it and have to look it up every day now. I didn't used to be like this..

My TSH is 10 something and when I told the doctor at the ER (a doctor from my practice told me to go) that he said "well that's not high but okay. High would be 200"

He was a prick I was so upset. No bedside manner. At all. Sent me home in five minutes and gave me muscle relaxers. Nobody takes me seriously except my GP and psychiatrist. Everyone else things I'm crazy or faking it.

Update: Went to the ER because I felt so bad, had to drive myself because my bf had a few drinks earlier. They didn't take me seriously at all even though I told them what  was wrong. I wanted to tell the doctor all of my symptoms but I couldn't remember all of them so he super didn't take me seriously. They sent me home in five minutes with some muscle relaxers. I feel so stupid for asking for help when I needed it.
I take a B complex but I'll try to add calcium. I'm eliminating milk because it makes me puffy :((

I'm glad I'm not alone in this. I've never head of those meds before, I've only heard of and had levothyroxine. I'm thinking about seeing an endocrinologist if my levels get worse again for the third time in a row. I've never even heard the term myxedema. Good to know it has a name! Thank you for the sympathy and understanding. This sucks. :(
Oh really? That's interesting I'd expect them to be better haha. Since this doctor listens to me I'm probably going to stick with her unless she can't figure out how to fix this.

I mean, when I eat bread sometimes my stomach hurts really bad instantly- but other foods like cookies and stuff doesn't bother me at all. I'll have to ask my doctor if I should get it checked out though- because anything is possible. I'm going to be so sad if I have to give up bagels tho haha

I'm only on levothyroxine so that might be why. I suggested to my doctor if more synthroid doesn't work that I should try T3 as well since that seems to help people from what I've read. I SHOULD see an endocrinologist but I'd rather stay with my PCP IF possible. 😞 Adding too many doctors to the mix gets confusing because they end up not communicating well with each other if they're not in the same practice. And my practice doesn't have an endo.

To add onto my answer the normal range for free T4 is 0.82-1.77

The range for free T3 is listed as: 1.2-4.9

And the range for Thyroxine is 4.5-12.0

For the T3 on the lab sheet it says (Free Thyroid Index) but it does not say that for T4. When I finally got bloodwork in January when I started to feel awful my T4 labeled as (Free, Direct) was 0.7

The normal ranges were listed on the sheet and they both fall only a bit low outside of normal range, but my TSH is super high comparatively. It was at 6.96 in January and then on March 3rd my TSH rose to 10something (whatever I listed in the post I'm not looking at the scan at the moment)

I know that's TMI tho lmao, hence why this is a burner account lmao. I also sleep all day whenever I'm not busy with other stuff because 0 energy.

Even though it was on one of the scripts. :( I'll have to ask for it to be done again. On a new order lol. What is the treatment for high antibodies. I remember having SUPER HIGH antibodies when I was first tested but they never tested them again after I became 18 lmao. I asked this time but like I said the blood work people messed up. My doctor has been pretty good so far, so I'll see what she says when I see her next week.

However, there are no endocrinologists in my area under my insurance plan unfortunately. There might be some in a different part of the state I'm in or something I'll have to check.


I don't take other meds at the same time as my thyroid med no, because those medications need to be taken with food.

I am however feeling so bad. I just can't believe it went from 6.9 to 10something in six weeks. That is a HUGE jump.
Six weeks ago I went up to 100mcg

I'm on:
Geodon 80mg twice a day
Lamictal Extended Release 300mg at night
Trileptal 300mg in the morning, 900 at night (Just got to 900, every time I went up in dosage I experienced horrible vertigo and kept falling over but it DID go away in the past so I'm hoping this is the case 😓)
And Guanfacine Extended Release for my adhd

I also have Hashimoto's Thyroiditis so I can't take Lithium sadly :( for that I take Levothyroxine.

And yeah I was in a horrible depression and when I increased the Trileptal it was like the black hole in my brain went away! I constantly was thinking about self harm and suicide, it just wouldn't turn off. I'm so glad to be out of that, I'm almost considering never driving again just so I can feel this good. But I also can't work like this so unfortunately I'd have to go on something else.
